title: Inorder Traversal
statement: Print the inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree.
inputOutputContract: Input n followed by n BST-insertion values; equal values enter the right subtree. Output inorder traversal values separated by spaces.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the preorder instead of inorder behavior in inorder / insert; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T1 manually. Watch TreeNode / root / left / right at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of inorder / insert: Insert BST nodes by value and recursively visit left subtree, root, then right subtree.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `printf("%s%d", *first ? "" : " ", root->val); *first = 0; inorder(root->left, first);`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T1. The mistake is in preorder instead of inorder, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Insert BST nodes by value and recursively visit left subtree, root, then right subtree.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `printf("%s%d", *first ? "" : " ", root->val); *first = 0; inorder(root->left, first);` with `inorder(root->left, first); printf("%s%d", *first ? "" : " ", root->val); *first = 0;` in inorder / insert, then retest T1–T6.
